originalGroup.material:
Wrong Garden Gate Story 018

On her first day at the music club, Esme followed a violin sound down a narrow lane. She found a green gate and waited. No one opened it. She was about to go home when an old man came out carrying gardening gloves. He had been listening to a radio. The violin she had followed was not a lesson.
Esme showed him the club message on paper. It said "Garden Hall, east gate." She had remembered only the word "garden." The man pointed to a building beyond the lane. Its east gate faced the next street. Esme thanked him and arrived ten minutes late. The teacher welcomed her and asked her to read the whole direction next time. At the end of the lesson, she wrote a small arrow on her copy of the message. She kept the friendly mistake as a reminder that a familiar word was not the whole instruction.

originalGroup.material:
Bicycle Coat Rain Story 018

Noah left his bicycle outside the evening class. When the lesson ended, rain was falling hard. Someone had wrapped an old coat around his seat. He felt grateful and searched for the owner, but the street was nearly empty. A woman at the next doorway said that an elderly man had passed by with a cart.
Noah cycled after the man and offered the coat back. The man looked surprised. He had covered the seat because a small cloth bag was hanging below it, open to the rain. Noah had not noticed that his bag zip was undone. The coat had protected his sketchbook as well as the seat.
Noah asked how to repay him. The man said the coat had been in his cart on its way to a repair shop; it was not rubbish. He gladly took it back and accepted Noah’s help pushing the cart over a rough patch. Noah rode home with dry drawings and a changed idea of the small favour he had received.

He felt grateful and searched for the owner, but the street was nearly empty. A woman at the next doorway said that an elderly man had passed by with a cart.
Noah cycled after the man and offered the coat back. The man looked surprised. He had covered the seat because a small cloth bag was hanging below it, open to the rain. Noah had not noticed that his bag zip was undone. The coat had protected his sketchbook as well as the seat.
Noah asked how to repay him. The man said the coat had been in his cart on its way to a repair shop; it was not rubbish. He gladly took it back and accepted Noah’s help pushing the cart over a rough patch. Noah rode home with dry drawings and a changed idea of the small favour he had received.

originalGroup.material:
Missing Comic Page Letter 018

Dear Hana,
I thought I had damaged your comic when I found a missing page. I was ready to buy a new copy before telling you. Then I checked the photo you had sent when you lent it to me. The page edge in that photo already looked torn. I still could not be certain from the small picture, so I wrote to ask rather than deciding for myself. You explained that the page had fallen out last year and was kept safely in a folder. I was relieved. We agreed to store the loose page with the book before lending it again. Next time, I will check a borrowed item’s condition at the start and tell its owner promptly about a concern, instead of quietly assuming either blame or innocence.
Best,
Ari
